source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 4 (The Deccan Schools of Painting).

sections.heading: 1. Deccan Painting — Context
points: **Deccan painting** developed in the **Deccan Sultanates** — **Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda** (16th–17th c.).
It blended **indigenous Deccan, Persian, Turkish and later Mughal** influences.
It flourished **independently of, and partly before, full Mughal influence**.

sections.heading: 2. Major Centres and Features
points: **Ahmadnagar** — early Deccan painting (e.g. the **Tarif-i-Hussain Shahi**).
**Bijapur** — under **Ibrahim Adil Shah II** (a great patron, himself a musician); rich, lyrical paintings; the **Ragamala** and portraits.
**Golconda** — prosperous; refined paintings, court scenes, lavish use of gold and rich colour.
Features: **rich, glowing colours, lavish gold, dreamy and lyrical quality, distinctive costumes and landscapes**.

sections.heading: 3. Later Deccan Painting
points: After the Mughal conquest of the Deccan (late 17th c.), the style absorbed more **Mughal influence**.
**Hyderabad** became a later centre under the **Nizams**.
Deccan painting retained a distinct **colour sense and romantic charm** even under Mughal influence.

sections.heading: 4. Significance
points: Deccan painting is prized for its **individuality, opulence and poetic mood**.
It shows the Deccan's cosmopolitan culture (Persian, Turkish, African, Indian).
It is a distinct branch of Indian miniature painting, alongside the Mughal, Rajasthani and Pahari.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Deccan schools: Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda (Deccan Sultanates).
Bijapur flourished under Ibrahim Adil Shah II (patron and musician).
Features: rich glowing colours, lavish gold, lyrical/dreamy quality.
Later centre = Hyderabad (under the Nizams).
Blended indigenous Deccan + Persian/Turkish + Mughal influences.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Deccan painting = Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda** (the Deccan Sultanates).
**Ibrahim Adil Shah II (Bijapur)** was a great patron of the arts and music.
Deccan painting is known for **rich colour and lavish gold** (lyrical mood).
**Hyderabad (Nizams)** was a **later** Deccan painting centre.
